compressed-bytes-depend-on-the-zlib-buil: `build` steps record the sha256, size and base64 of what buildOverlayTarGz returns, which is gzip level 9 output from Node's zlib. The same tar compressed by Rust's flate2 (miniz_oxide or zlib-ng) can differ byte for byte, and a Node upgrade can move the TS bytes too. The decompressed tar is the stable part: tarSize and tarSha256 are compared byte for byte, and so are the gzip header fields the writer pins (mtime 0, OS byte 3) and the tar header fields in buildHeader. The replay compares size and sha256 of the compressed bytes only when the Rust writer reports the same deflate implementation; otherwise it requires the gunzipped tar to equal the golden's tar and the compressed output to be a valid gzip stream that readOverlayTarGz accepts.
gunzip-error-text: A gunzip failure (not gzip, beyond the byte cap) reads `overlay archive: gunzip failed or exceeded <N> bytes (<message>)` with zlib's own message in the parentheses, which differs between zlib builds and from the Rust decoder's. The golden records the token <ZLIB-MESSAGE>; the replay compares everything up to and including 'bytes (' and requires a non-empty message and the closing parenthesis.
read-inputs-are-stored-gzip: Every archive a `read` step carries is gzip with stored blocks (level 0) and the xfl and OS header bytes pinned to 0 and 3, written by the oracle's own ustar encoder, so the input bytes do not move with Node's zlib. The reader's verdict does not depend on the compression level.
entry-smaller-than-the-pinned-size-is-ac: Recorded as found (D-20), see .planning/todos/pending/2026-11-25-overlay-archive-reader-accepts-an-entry-smaller-than-its-pin.md. The Rust reader replays it as recorded.
